title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
content: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member on November 12, effective immediately, the company's board said. He had led the company for 33 years, since its founding.

title: Micron says it has not required waivers and will keep negotiating in Taoyuan labor dispute
content: Micron Technology has responded to an open letter from the Taoyuan Union, a labor group in Taiwan, about its ongoing contract talks. Taoyuan is a city in northern Taiwan where Micron has a large factory, and the dispute centers on a new employee bonus program that the union has been pressing the company to discuss.

title: Quanta shifts 2027 capex toward power, the new battleground for AI server ODMs
content: Quanta Computer posted strong revenue and earnings in the third quarter of 2026 and expects operations to continue accelerating in the fourth quarter, driven by AI servers. The company also forecasts another growth year in 2027, planning capital expenditure (capex) of NT$40 billion (US$1.21 billion) to NT$45 billion, although it says spending will begin to moderate.

title: Pegatron targets multiyear AI server surge, with Nvidia Vera Rubin shipments set for 1H27
content: Pegatron said at its November 12 earnings briefing that 2026 would mark its first year of server shipments, with the business expected to contribute about 10% of consolidated revenue and grow severalfold in 2027. Its portfolio spans Nvidia's GB series and HGX platforms, as well as custom ASIC servers, while shipments of next-generation Vera Rubin systems are expected to begin in the first half of 2027.

title: Foxconn sees high-double-digit AI rack growth in 2027
content: Foxconn reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of more than NT$3 trillion (US$91 billion) and raised its full-year outlook, while taking a "cautiously optimistic" view of 2027 and forecasting high-double-digit growth in AI rack shipments. The company expects to gain market share through diversified AI solutions and an expanding customer base, but warned that component supplies, geopolitical and economic conditions, inflation, and monetary policy will shape its 2027 operations.

title: Aleees makes Tainan plant launchpad for North American LFP expansion
content: Advanced Lithium Electrochemistry (Aleees), a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode-material maker, signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with a North American partner on November 12 to trial-produce LFP cathode materials through a joint venture, as demand for power batteries and energy storage rises and Europe and the US accelerate supply-chain localization.

title: Chinese universities obtain Nvidia chips despite US export controls
content: Several Chinese universities, including Northwestern Polytechnical University, one of China's "Seven Sons of National Defense," have successfully obtained Nvidia chips despite US export controls, according to Reuters. Procurement records show the university purchased two Nvidia H200 chips for CNY875,000 (approximately US$177,629) through a domestic supplier rather than directly from Nvidia.

title: Naver signs US$1.5 billion AI cloud deal with US firm
content: Naver said on November 12 it had signed a KRW2 trillion (approx. US$1.5 billion) AI computing services contract with a US-based AI inference company, securing its first major customer for the AI Factory business it is developing with Nvidia and Brookfield.

title: India's Tata Electronics reportedly seeks up to US$2 billion in loans
content: Tata Electronics is lining up fresh debt at a moment when nearly every leg of its expansion has run into friction: a flagship chip fab whose production start has moved from the end of 2026 to mid-2028 and will launch on an older process, losses that widened even as revenue doubled, and a run of incidents at its iPhone component plant in Tamil Nadu.

title: Synnex pivots to AI solution enabler, targets continued growth in 2027
content: Synnex Technology International Corp. posted record quarterly revenue in the third quarter of 2026 and expects continued growth and new highs in 2027, driven by AI semiconductors, AI servers and infrastructure, and its China AI server business. The company is also launching fundraising plans, including a cash capital increase, CD issuance and expanded bank credit lines, to meet its funding needs.

title: China's AI short-drama boom opens new token revenue opportunity for ByteDance's Seedance, Volcengine
content: China's AI-generated short-drama market is expanding rapidly, with surging content production and viewership making the sector an increasingly significant source of demand for AI computing resources.

title: SoftBank rejects Musk's default claim, books JPY597.2B data-center loss
content: SoftBank Group (SBG) has denied SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's claim on X that the company defaulted after ordering turbines, while saying its AI infrastructure plans remain on track. However, SBG recorded a JPY597.2 billion (US$3.73 billion) loss in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 (July–September 2026) after reviewing purchases of power-generation equipment for US data centers, though it said the loss was unrelated to Project Stargate Ohio.

title: Amtran's 3Q26 profit tops 1H26 total as non-TV shipments surge
content: Amtran Technology reported a sharp profit increase in the third quarter of 2026, driven by stronger shipments of high-value non-TV products and an optimized product mix. Third-quarter earnings per share reached NT$0.59 (US$0.018), up 103% quarter-over-quarter, while earnings for the first three quarters rose 27% year-over-year to NT$1.03 per share.

title: Sam Altman warns Samsung of short-term AI demand volatility
content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman warned Samsung Electronics executives that AI memory demand could fluctuate in the short term, with the market potentially counting the same demand more than once. He nevertheless expects long-term AI demand to surge, creating shortages of chips and data centers and underscoring the need for greater supply chain investment.

title: Chinese media question timing of Huang allegations amid chip controls
content: With Chinese and US leaders expected to meet on October 18 during the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, allegations involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair and supposed links to Chinese espionage continue to escalate. China's state-run Global Times questioned whether the closely timed media reports and congressional actions reflect political maneuvering behind US technology policy toward China.

title: Meta infrastructure chief to hand over AI compute role in 2027
content: Meta Platforms' longtime infrastructure chief Santosh Janardhan will leave after the end of 1Q27, with former Amazon Web Services (AWS) vice president Dave Brown set to succeed him. The leadership transition comes as Meta accelerates its AI strategy and expands data centers and in-house chip development.

title: Kwang-Hwa swings to profit in 3Q26 as EPF film line nears launch
content: Kwang-Hwa Electronic reported consolidated revenue of NT$1.315 billion in the third quarter of 2026, down 2.78% quarter-on-quarter and 3.01% year-on-year. Gross profit was NT$324 million, up 8.61% quarter-on-quarter but down 9.07% year-on-year. Supported by foreign-exchange gains, the company swung to a net profit attributable to its parent of NT$1.98 million, or NT$0.03 per share.

title: Taiwan's electronics industry targets four overseas tech parks under TEEMA's global expansion plan
content: The Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association (TEEMA) released its first industry white paper in 78 years on November 11, proposing a "Taiwan+N" global expansion strategy centred on overseas technology parks, supply chain integration and stronger domestic manufacturing capabilities.
